title: AI Representations of Mental Health Stigma: Quantifying the Gap Between AI Estimations and Human Perceptions Across Gender Groups Using GPT-Based LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2610.16042v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in mental health applications raises concerns about its potential to internalize and perpetuate societal biases. This research evaluates both disparities and misalignment in how large language models (LLMs), GPT-4 and GPT-5, represent perceptions of mental health across gender groups. The research comprises two studies. Study 1 applied widely adopted measures of Social Distance, Stereotypes, and Attitudes Toward Seeking Help to assess whether the AI models depict systematic gender differences. Study 2 compared AI estimations of Personal, Self, and Perceived Stigma with large-scale real-world human data from the Healthy Minds Study (N = 76,406) to evaluate alignment between AI estimations and human perceptions. Results from Study 1 showed the AI models consistently portrayed men as having the greatest desire for social distance from someone with mental health problems, relatively higher

translated_title: AI对心理健康污名的表征：基于GPT大语言模型量化AI估计与人类感知在不同性别群体间的差距
translated_abstract: 人工智能（AI）在心理健康应用中的日益普及，引发了人们对其可能内化并延续社会偏见的担忧。本研究评估了大型语言模型（GPT-4和GPT-5）在表征不同性别群体心理健康感知时所呈现的差异与错位。该研究包含两项研究。研究一采用广泛使用的社交距离、刻板印象和求助态度测量工具，评估AI模型是否描绘出系统性的性别差异。研究二将AI对个人污名、自我污名和感知污名的估计，与来自Healthy Minds Study的大规模真实人类数据（样本量N = 76,406）进行对比，以评估AI估计与人类感知之间的一致性。研究一的结果显示，AI模型一致地将男性描绘为对心理健康问题患者保持最大社交距离愿望的群体，相对更高……
tldr: 本研究首次通过两项实证研究，量化了GPT-4和GPT-5大语言模型在表征心理健康污名时存在的系统性性别差异，并利用超过7.6万份真实人类数据揭示了AI估计与人类感知之间的错位程度。
en_tdlr: This study quantifies systematic gender disparities in how GPT-4 and GPT-5 LLMs represent mental health stigma and measures the misalignment between AI estimations and large-scale real-world human perception data.
